audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Elihu's first direct address to Job: appeal to shared clay, claim that God speaks through dreams and suffering, messenger/mediator imagery, ransom language, restoration, and Elihu's invitation for reply.

verses.restored: But now, Job, please hear my words, and listen to all my speech.

familiar.text: Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.

verses.restored: Look, I have opened my mouth; my tongue has spoken in my palate.

familiar.text: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.

verses.restored: My words are from the uprightness of my heart, and my lips speak knowledge clearly.

familiar.text: My words shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.

verses.restored: The Spirit of the Divine has made me, and the breath of Shaddai gives me life.

familiar.text: The spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.

verses.restored: If you are able, answer me; arrange yourself before me, take your stand.

familiar.text: If thou canst answer me, set thy words in order before me, stand up.

verses.restored: Look, I am like you before the Divine; I too was pinched off from clay.

familiar.text: Behold, I am according to thy wish in God’s stead: I also am formed out of the clay.

verses.restored: Look, my terror will not frighten you, and my pressure will not be heavy upon you.

familiar.text: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.

verses.restored: Surely you have spoken in my ears, and I have heard the sound of words:

familiar.text: Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words, saying,

verses.restored: I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no guilt in me.

familiar.text: I am clean without transgression, I am innocent; neither is there iniquity in me.

verses.restored: Look, he finds occasions against me; he counts me as his enemy.

familiar.text: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,

verses.restored: He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths.

familiar.text: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.

verses.restored: Look, in this you are not right, I answer you, for the Divine is greater than a mortal.

familiar.text: Behold, in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.

verses.restored: Why do you contend against him, saying that he answers none of a person’s words?

familiar.text: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.

verses.restored: For the Divine speaks in one way, and in two, though a person does not perceive it.

familiar.text: For God speaketh once, yea twice, yet man perceiveth it not.

verses.restored: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people, while they slumber on the bed,

familiar.text: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;

verses.restored: then he opens the ear of people and seals their instruction,

familiar.text: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,

verses.restored: to turn a person from deed, and hide pride from a man.

familiar.text: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.

verses.restored: He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from crossing the weapon.

familiar.text: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.

verses.restored: He is also corrected with pain on his bed, and with continual strife in his bones,

familiar.text: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong pain:

verses.restored: so that his life loathes bread, and his soul desirable food.

familiar.text: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat.

verses.restored: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his bones once unseen are exposed.

familiar.text: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones that were not seen stick out.

verses.restored: His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to those who bring death.

familiar.text: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.

verses.restored: If there is for him a messenger, a mediator, one out of a thousand, to declare to a human what is right for him,

familiar.text: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:

verses.restored: then he is gracious to him and says, Ransom him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom.

familiar.text: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.

verses.restored: His flesh becomes fresher than a child’s; he returns to the days of his youth.

familiar.text: His flesh shall be fresher than a child’s: he shall return to the days of his youth:

verses.restored: He prays to the Divine, and the Divine accepts him; he sees his face with a shout of joy, and he restores to a person his righteousness.

familiar.text: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.

verses.restored: He sings before people and says, I sinned and twisted what was right, but it was not repaid to me.

familiar.text: He looketh upon men, and if any say, I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it profited me not;

verses.restored: He redeemed my soul from passing into the pit, and my life shall see the light.

familiar.text: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.

verses.restored: Look, all these the Divine does, two times, three times with a person,

familiar.text: Lo, all these things worketh God oftentimes with man,

verses.restored: to bring back his soul from the pit, to be illumined with the light of life.

familiar.text: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.

verses.restored: Pay attention, Job; listen to me. Be silent, and I myself will speak.

familiar.text: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.

verses.restored: If you have words, answer me; speak, for I desire to justify you.

familiar.text: If thou hast anything to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.

verses.restored: If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.

familiar.text: If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.
